issues.legal_issue: The alleged loan, supporting document, arbitration award, and resulting decree were fictitious and collusive rather than genuine evidence of a debt supporting the claim to attached property.
material_facts: The alleged creditor relied on an agreement said to acknowledge a substantial debt and create a mortgage, but it was neither stamped nor registered.
The agreement included a disposition of property in favour of the debtor’s cousin and made no provision for the debtor’s wife, who had been given broad rights over the property in a registered will.

The alleged creditor’s estate was managed by a public authority, yet no account records substantiating the alleged transactions were produced, and the creditor said substantial sums had been paid without obtaining receipts.
The sums claimed in the agreement, award, and interest calculation did not reconcile with one another.
The person who signed the agreement as the debtor’s agent was also selected as arbitrator but was not examined; the award, suit, and consent to a decree followed in rapid succession.
issues.conclusion: The Court agreed that the alleged lending and the proceedings from the agreement through the decree were fictitious and collusive, and dismissed the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the surrounding circumstances and documentary and oral evidence together, finding that the circumstances outweighed the supporting testimony. Although the dispute arose from a suit under Order 21, Rule 63 of the Code of Civil Procedure following a claim under Order 21, Rule 58, the Court stated that it was unnecessary to discuss points of law. It relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: appeal_in_attached_property_claim_suit and litigation_oriented_debt_document and unsupported_or_inconsistent_loan_evidence and rapid_arbitration_and_consent_decree

predicates.appeal_in_attached_property_claim_suit: A party appeals from a judgment in a suit challenging another person’s successful claim to property attached in execution.
predicates.litigation_oriented_debt_document: The alleged debtor and creditor used a debt document whose terms or timing indicated that it was prepared to support a competing claim to property rather than to secure an ordinary loan.
predicates.unsupported_or_inconsistent_loan_evidenc: The alleged lender produced no reliable account or receipts for substantial advances, or the amounts and interest stated in the loan and later proceedings did not reconcile.
predicates.rapid_arbitration_and_consent_decree: The person involved in preparing the alleged debt document also participated in the arbitration, and an award and consent decree followed in unusually rapid succession.

issues.definition: When an appeal in an attached-property claim suit involves a litigation-oriented debt document, unsupported or inconsistent loan evidence, and rapid arbitration and decree proceedings, the alleged debt and enforcement proceedings are treated as fictitious and collusive.

issues.legal_issue: The evidence did not establish that the debtor and his cousin belonged to a joint Hindu family.
material_facts: The alleged family members were cousins rather than brothers.
They lived in different villages and managed the lands in those villages separately.
The claim that they were joint rested on oral testimony, with no other evidence establishing joint status.
The surrounding proceedings indicated that the asserted relationship was used to support a claim to the debtor’s property.
issues.conclusion: The Court agreed that the evidence of joint status was worthless and did not establish that the two men were joint.
issues.legal_principle: The Court evaluated the oral testimony against the circumstances and the lack of other evidence, concluding that testimony from several witnesses alone did not establish joint status in this case. It cited no statutory provision or earlier case for this conclusion and stated that it was unnecessary to discuss points of law.

rule.if: appeal_in_attached_property_claim_suit and relatives_are_cousins and relatives_live_and_manage_property_separately and joint_status_lacks_independent_support

predicates.appeal_in_attached_property_claim_suit: A party appeals from a judgment in a suit challenging another person’s successful claim to property attached in execution.
predicates.relatives_are_cousins: The people alleged to form a joint family are cousins rather than brothers.
predicates.relatives_live_and_manage_property_separ: The alleged family members live in different places and separately manage the properties associated with those places.
predicates.joint_status_lacks_independent_support: The claim of joint status rests on oral testimony without other evidence supporting it.

issues.definition: When an appeal in an attached-property claim suit concerns cousins who live and manage property separately and the claim of joint status lacks independent support, joint-family status is not established.
